faq_schema.q: What age is best for spot the difference puzzles?
faq_schema.a: Children as young as 4 can start with simple puzzles (3-5 differences). By age 12, they can handle complex images with subtle changes. Our Animals Vol.4 set works for all these ages.

faq_schema.q: How is spot the difference different from hidden pictures?
faq_schema.a: Hidden pictures require finding specific items in a cluttered scene, which can overwhelm some kids. Spot the difference compares two similar images, teaching systematic comparison—a key reading skill.

faq_schema.q: Can spot the difference puzzles help with dyslexia?
faq_schema.a: Yes! They build visual discrimination, which is often weak in dyslexic readers. Regular practice can improve letter and word recognition.

faq_schema.q: How many differences should a puzzle have for a 7-year-old?
faq_schema.a: 7-year-olds typically handle 5-7 differences. Our Animals Vol.4 includes puzzles with varying difficulty to match each child's level.

faq_schema.q: Are these puzzles good for ESL learners?
faq_schema.a: Absolutely. The photorealistic animal images build vocabulary and encourage verbal descriptions. Each puzzle becomes a language lesson as well.
